checklists.intro: Longer, practical, translated guides for migrant women and their supporters — boarding, travel, safety, health and recovery.
checklists.for_friends: For friends / family: How to safely help
checklists.for_you: If you are in crisis right now: Step by step
checklists.for_mothers: Checklist for mothers traveling or escaping with children
for_friends_items: Listen calmly without judging. Reassure her it is never her fault.
Do not pressure or rush her. Allow her the time and agency to decide her course.
Together create a quick safety plan. Note exit routes, trusted contacts and locations of key documents.
Volunteer to safely hold copies of IDs, passports or important docs for her.
Help drive/escort to legal or medical appointments if it is completely safe.
Keep strict confidentiality. Never share details of her situation without explicit permission.
Offer to research shelters and hotlines together on her personal safe device only.
Help her explore financial possibilities, reimbursement, welfare supports in her language.
for_you_items: Assemble a hidden small escape bag containing cash, meds, copies of documents.
Store critical phone numbers in your head + saved privately (emergency + shelters).
Scout two exit routes from your home. Identify a secondary safe meetup spot.
Choose one person you can communicate with on a predictable safe schedule.
Turn off unnecessary location services. Check for unknown apps or spyware.
If you must flee, turn off all devices early and delete browsing data or carry device off.
Seek specialized legal advice early concerning custody, immigration & visa rights, and housing.
Protect passwords and email – change them on a trusted device when opportunity occurs.
Make an emergency code phrase with close trusted friends that can trigger safe rescue action.
for_mothers_items: Include baby/toddler essentials: diapers, rehydration, small toys, meds in bag. Keep list.
Carry photocopies or digital backups of each child’s birth cert, vaccinations and custody papers.
Pack a carrier or sling for you to hold young ones with hands free when quick movement required.
Choose women-only shelters with child policy or onsite day care / medical services.
Look for emergency formula/food in local community centers near your destination.
Prioritize registration of children at arrival: asylum or school placement protects them later.
Calm children using routine and storytime — most shelters offer psychological care for kids.
Memorize children’s date of birth + passport data and the emergency number to call.
Plan to inform only childcare or health personnel. Reduce exposure of your location to outsiders.

footer: Leave this site safely at any time using the Leave button. This does not erase records held by your network provider or device.

chat.option_no_documents: I have no documents / passport withheld

chat.nodocs: Stay safe – many shelters can help you with new IDs later. Consult with a trusted advisor by phone when you can.
chat.legal: Legal supports may assist with protective orders, custody, housing rights and immigration relief. Many places have free services for immigrant women.

option.safety_now: I am in danger right now

safety.danger_now: Are you currently in immediate danger?
safety.danger_advice: Get to safety right now. Call local emergency services if possible (112/911 or country equivalent). Use the quick exit if needed. Find the nearest safe shelter on the map.
safety.threats_advice: Document the threats if safe to do so. Go to a public safe place. Contact local police or a women's shelter. Consider an emergency protection order.
safety.control_advice: Prepare a safety plan quietly. Keep contacts and important documents hidden. Find safe housing options immediately.
safety.stalking_desc: You are being followed or stalked.
safety.stalking_advice: Change routes and routines. Inform trusted people. Use safe locations and seek legal protection.
safety.digital_advice: Use a safe device. Change passwords from a secure place. Turn off location sharing and check installed apps carefully.
safety.financial_advice: Secretly find work options if possible or support from organizations. Ask for financial aid line from shelters or NGOs.
safety.docs_advice: Contact organizations that help migrant women regain documents. Plan the moment to leave carefully.

docs.lost_passport_advice: Report the loss to your embassy/consulate and local police (if safe). Shelters often help with replacement. You may be able to travel with a temporary document.
docs.lost_child_advice: Contact the embassy of the country of citizenship of the children. Shelters and social services can assist with temporary papers.
docs.held_desc: Documents are being held by someone.
docs.held_advice: This is often a sign of control or trafficking. Contact a specialized helpline or shelter for migrant women immediately.
docs.expired_advice: Different procedures apply per country regarding renewal or regularization. Many NGOs provide free legal help to migrants.
docs.status_desc: I do not understand my residence status.
docs.status_advice: Seek free legal migration advice. Many refugee and migrant support organizations can clarify your rights.
docs.escape_no_docs_desc: Step-by-step checklist: how to safely leave when your original documents are taken or locked away.
docs.escape_no_docs_advice: Detailed step-by-step guide is currently available in Russian. Please switch language to Русский to read the full checklist, or ask a Russian-speaking helper to translate it for you. Summary: your life is the priority — leave first, documents can be restored later; if possible, secretly photograph passport pages and send them to yourself; leave under an everyday pretext; go to a busy public place with security cameras and ask staff to call the police; file a police report and ask for a written receipt (it temporarily replaces your passport); then contact your consulate to obtain a return certificate.

housing.nowhere_desc: You have nowhere to live right now.
housing.nowhere_advice: Use the help map to find shelters and crisis centers accepting women (including migrants). Call them before going if possible.
housing.temp_advice: Women's shelters and migrant support centers often have emergency beds. Use the filters on the map.
housing.evicted_desc: You are being or have been evicted.
housing.evicted_advice: Legal aid for eviction cases is available in many countries. Shelters can help while you solve next steps.
housing.conflict_advice: If threats or danger are involved, treat as safety issue. Otherwise local housing organizations and legal help can intervene.
housing.crisis_desc: You need a crisis center right now.
housing.crisis_advice: Search on the map using the 'shelter' or 'crisis' filters. Call a national helpline for women for immediate referral.

work.what_issue: What problem have you encountered at work?
work.no_pay_advice: Document everything (contracts, hours, communications). Contact labor inspectorate or a migrant workers' legal service. Some women's organizations have worker rights programs.
work.docs_held_advice: This is a serious warning sign (often related to trafficking or exploitation). Contact specialized services immediately.
work.forced_desc: You are being forced to work.
work.forced_advice: This can be forced labor. Seek a safe place first (shelter). Then contact law enforcement or anti-trafficking organizations when safe.
work.discr_advice: Labor law and anti-discrimination bodies protect you. Keep records. Seek legal advice from migrant-friendly organizations.
work.fired_advice: Maintain calm communications in writing. Request reasons in writing. Consult legal aid focused on migrants before signing anything.
work.unsafe_advice: You have the right to refuse dangerous work. Contact labor protection inspectorate and a women's/migrant service.

psych.feeling: What are you feeling right now?
psych.anx_advice: Breathing exercises and grounding techniques can help short-term. Many shelters and NGOs have psychologists or groups for migrant women. You are not alone.
psych.fear_advice: Create an immediate safety plan. Reach out to a trusted helpline. Professional support is available in your languages in many places.
psych.lonely_advice: Community groups and women's spaces for migrants exist in many cities. Ask around on the help map for women support circles.
psych.stress_advice: Stress is normal. Many centers offer integration support and psychological first aid for migrant and refugee women.
psych.burn_advice: Rest when possible. Seek low-pressure support. Organizations specializing in migrant women often have mental health peer support.

child.what_worries: What concerns you regarding your child?
child.safety_desc: You are worried about your child's safety.
child.safety_advice: Prioritize reaching a safe shelter or service that accommodates mothers with children. Many do.
child.edu_desc: Education and schooling for the child.
child.edu_note: School enrollment rules vary by country and region. It is recommended to contact the local education authority or the school directly to clarify the list of required documents.
child.med_advice: Many women's shelters and migrant services have links to pediatric care or free/low-cost clinics that understand migrants' situations.
child.docs_desc: Child is missing or has incomplete documents.
child.docs_advice: Embassies, consulates, and many NGOs help mothers restore or obtain children's papers.
child.psych_advice: Trauma-informed organizations for children of migrant families exist in many locations. Shelters can often refer.

legal.which: What legal issue do you need help with?
legal.mig_desc: Problems with migration or residence status.
legal.mig_advice: Find free specialized legal aid for migrants and refugees. Many countries have pro bono or NGO lawyers who regularly assist women migrants.
legal.labor_desc: Labor rights problem (non-payment, unsafe conditions, exploitation).
legal.labor_advice: Contact the national labor inspectorate and organizations that defend migrant workers. Keep written records.
legal.fam_advice: Seek family law advice from organizations that understand migrant women's realities, including custody and divorce proceedings.
legal.disc_advice: Anti-discrimination bodies and human rights organizations can provide support and legal recourse.
legal.child_prot_advice: Contact child protection services (social services) and reputable NGOs. In shelters this is usually assisted.
legal.restore_desc: Need to restore or replace documents.
legal.restore_advice: Start with the embassy/consulate of your country of citizenship plus local legal aid organizations for migrants.

medical.emerg_advice: Go to the nearest emergency department or call the local emergency number (112/999/911 depending on country). Shelters can help with transport and follow-up when you are safe.
medical.treat_desc: You require ongoing medical treatment or follow-up.
medical.treat_advice: Many NGOs and public health services have special programs or reduced fees for migrants and refugees. Ask at a shelter or health hotline for women.
medical.meds_advice: Ask pharmacies about generic alternatives or patient assistance programs. Clinics serving migrants often provide or prescribe at low cost.
medical.child_desc: Medical care needed for your child(ren).
medical.child_advice: Pediatric care in public systems is often available to children regardless of status. Women's and children's shelters can assist with admission.
medical.psych_advice: Psychological first aid and longer term counseling for survivors (including migrants) is provided by specialized women's centers and trauma services.

help.who_are_you: Who are you in relation to the person who needs help?
help.relative_advice: Listen calmly without judgment. Ask what help she needs right now. Help her quietly find resources while respecting her decisions. Keep strict confidentiality.
help.friend_advice: Listen without judgment. Ask what kind of help she needs. Help locate resources. Respect privacy and decisions.
help.neighbour_advice: Offer practical short-term help (transport to safe place, childcare if short and safe). Point her toward women's services without taking over.
help.volunteer_advice: Provide accurate information. Help navigate available services. Refer to professionals when needed. Never promise what you cannot deliver.
help.teacher_advice: Support the child while being careful with confidentiality. Share information with trusted school counselors or child protection if there is imminent danger. Help the family find specialized support services.
help.employer_advice: Complete owed payments immediately. Do not hold documents under any circumstances. If you suspect exploitation or trafficking, contact the authorities and specialized anti-trafficking services. Facilitate access to help without coercion.

s2.adv_general_safety: Build a safety plan: save contacts of trusted people and shelters, prepare document copies, review the checklists. Find nearby centers on the help map.
s2.adv_prepare: While the aggressor is out, pack a bag with documents, money and essentials. Save trusted contacts and shelter numbers. Prepare an exit plan.
s2.adv_close_no: If you can't close the site fast — use incognito mode or someone else's device. You can always tap Quick Exit in the top right.
s2.adv_pw_relatives: Make sure relatives are ready to welcome you with the children and understand the situation. Agree in advance.
s2.adv_pw_friends: Make sure friends are ready to welcome you with the children. Agree on keys and details in advance.
s2.adv_pw_crisis: Crisis centers welcome women with children 24/7 and free of charge. Find the nearest one on the help map.
s2.adv_pw_shelter: Shelters provide safe housing free of charge. Find the nearest on the map.
s2.adv_pw_other: Make sure the place is truly safe and the aggressor doesn't know about it.
s2.adv_no_place: Many women's shelters and crisis centers accept women with children free of charge and urgently. Call a hotline — they will help find a place.
s2.adv_afraid: Shelters with confidential addresses exist where you cannot be found. Contact a women's organization — they will help.
s2.adv_wh_out: Discuss options with this person. They can help physically or morally at the moment of leaving.
s2.adv_wh_nobody: You are not alone — women's shelters, crisis lines and NGOs help exactly in these situations. Call a hotline.
s2.adv_tk_hear: Tap Quick Exit in the top right — the site will close instantly. Review the safety checklists. If possible, safely leave the room with the children.
s2.adv_leave_now: Leave for a safe place as soon as possible. Take documents and the children.
s2.adv_lock_room: Lock yourself with the children in a separate room, put the phone on speaker, call emergency services.
s2.adv_trust_adult: Reach out to a trusted adult. Ask them to stay with you or call for help.
s2.adv_call_hotline: Call a women's hotline or crisis center — they will help assess the situation and find help.
s2.adv_plan_kids: Build a family safety plan: a code word, safe places, contacts, what the children should do in danger. See the checklists.
s2.adv_check_kids: Reach the children in any safely available way. Make sure the adult with them is trustworthy.
s2.adv_check_kids_urgent: If you can't reach the children for more than a day — contact the police and social services. Also call a hotline.

about.title: Atlas Women
about.intro:
Atlas Women is an independent digital platform created to make information about available help for women clearer, more accessible and easier to use regardless of the country of residence.

The project focuses on gender safety, international migration and the role of digital technology in providing access to verified information.

Atlas Women is not a crisis centre, government agency or international organisation. The project independently collects, structures and publishes information from open, verifiable sources, helping users find existing support services in different countries faster.

Beyond the map of organisations, the platform includes research materials, anonymous women's stories and the ability to suggest new organisations for review and inclusion.
about.mission: To make verified information about help as accessible as possible and to show how digital technology can lower information barriers and support women's safety in the context of international migration.
about.includes:
an interactive world map of help organisations
a catalogue of crisis centres and support services
anonymous women's stories
research materials on migration, digital diplomacy and gender safety
the ability to suggest a new organisation
the ability to share your own story
about.principles:
accuracy of published information
respect for user privacy
openness and accessibility of information
independence of the project
continuous development and updating of the database
